title: The Only Reverse Sear Method You Need (Thick Ribeye)
creator: Smoke & Salt with Big Ray
description:
Two-inch ribeye, reverse seared on a kettle grill. Timings, temps, and how to not overcook a forty dollar steak.

MEATER: use code BIGRAY for 15% off at meater.com/bigray

My rub recipe: smokeandsaltbbq.com/rub
Kettle: 22 inch
Charcoal: lump, about half a chimney

sentences.t: Alright y'all, welcome back to the pit, today we're doing a big old ribeye, two inches thick, reverse sear.
If you've never done reverse sear, the idea is simple, you cook it low and slow first, then you hit it real hot at the end.
That way you get edge to edge pink instead of that grey band you get from searing first.
Now, I salted this steak last night and left it uncovered in the fridge, and look how dry that surface is.
That's what you want, dry surface means a better crust later.
I've got the kettle set up two-zone, coals all banked on one side, nothing on the other.
We're aiming for about two twenty five on the cool side.
Now I'm gonna take my MEATER probe here and push it right into the thickest part of the steak, sideways, all the way past that little line.
The nice thing is there's no wires, so I can close the lid and not have a cable pinched in there.
I'm pulling up the app on my phone, and I'll set the target to one twenty five, cause I want to pull it off the indirect side before the sear.
It's already reading ambient temp inside the grill too, so I can see it's sitting at about two thirty, which is right where we want it.
Okay, lid on, and now we wait.
